slides.title: Programs and environment
slides.main: A real program is a utility: parameters, log, exit codes, calling other programs.

slides.title: The sys module
slides.main: Errors go to stderr, data to stdout: so they separate when redirected.

body.text:

print(sys.argv[0] != "", type(sys.argv).__name__)
print(sys.version_info >= (3, 8), sys.platform in ("linux", "darwin", "win32"))
print("error", file=sys.stderr)
sys.stdout.write("to stdout\n")
print(isinstance(sys.path, list))

slides.title: argparse
slides.main: One description gives parsing, type checks and --help.

body.text:
import argparse

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Counter")
parser.add_argument("name", help="name")
parser.add_argument("--times", type=int, default=2, help="how many times")
parser.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
args = parser.parse_args(["Anna", "--times", "3", "-v"])
print(args.name, args.times, args.verbose)
print(parser.parse_args(["Boris"]))

slides.title: argparse techniques
slides.main: Subcommands: a separate parser per action, like git.

body.text:
import argparse

p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="tool")
p.add_argument("nums", nargs="+", type=int)
p.add_argument("--op", choices=["sum", "max"], default="sum")
a = p.parse_args(["3", "9", "4", "--op", "max"])
print(a.nums, a.op)
try:
    p.parse_args(["1", "--op", "avg"])
except SystemExit as e:
    print("exit with code", e.code)

slides.title: The os module
slides.main: Read environment variables with get: a missing setting must not crash the program.

body.text:
import os

os.environ["MODE"] = "test"
print(os.environ.get("MODE"), os.environ.get("MISSING", "—"))
print(os.getcwd() == os.path.abspath("."), (os.cpu_count() or 1) >= 1)
os.makedirs("a/b", exist_ok=True)
open("a/b/f.txt", "w").close()
for root, dirs, files in os.walk("a"):
    print(root, dirs, files)

slides.title: Input, output and return code
slides.main: A utility reading stdin and writing stdout chains with other programs in a pipeline.

body.text:
import io
import sys

fake = io.StringIO("10\n20\n30\n")      # instead of sys.stdin
total = sum(int(line) for line in fake)
print(total)
print("this is an error", file=sys.stderr)
print("return code", 0 if total else 1)

slides.title: logging
slides.main: DEBUG messages stay silent normally; to hunt a bug, just change the level.

body.text:
import logging
import sys

logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stdout, level=logging.INFO,
                    format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s", force=True)
logging.debug("hidden")
logging.info("start")
logging.warning("careful")
logging.error("failure")

INFO: start
WARNING: careful
ERROR: failure

slides.title: Loggers and handlers
slides.main: logger.exception() inside except logs the traceback; never log passwords.

body.text:
import logging
import sys

handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(name)s | %(levelname)s | %(message)s"))
log = logging.getLogger("app.db")
log.addHandler(handler)
log.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
log.propagate = False
log.debug("query")
try:
    1 / 0
except ZeroDivisionError as e:
    log.error("division: %s", e)

app.db | DEBUG | query
app.db | ERROR | division: division by zero

slides.title: Modules and packages
slides.main: An environment per project: no version conflicts.

body.text:
import importlib
import sys

print("antigravity" in sys.modules, "os" in sys.modules)
m = importlib.import_module("math")
print(m.__name__, m.sqrt(9))
print(__name__)
__init__.py makes a folder a package; python -m venv .venv is an isolated environment; pip or uv install packages.

slides.title: Typical mistakes
slides.sub: Data and errors in one stream, a silent log
slides.main: The return code is part of the interface: an error without non-zero code lies to the caller.

body.text:
import logging
import subprocess
import sys

print("data")
print("error", file=sys.stderr)
logging.basicConfig(stream=sys.stdout, level=logging.WARNING, format="%(message)s", force=True)
logging.info("hidden: the level is higher")
r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "pass"], capture_output=True)
print(r.stdout, r.returncode)
Also: passwords in the log, shell=True with user strings, no subprocess timeout, logging.basicConfig in a library.
